I see the issue now - the web_fetch tool call happens at the host level, and the result is returned as `_last_tool_result`, but the kernel doesn't automatically have access to it as a variable. I need to make the web_fetch call and the subsequent parsing happen in the SAME code block. Let me try that:

```python
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

# Make the web_fetch call and parse in the same block
r = web_fetch('https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2607.10798', max_chars=5000)

# Parse the returned content
root = ET.fromstring(r['content'])
ns = {'atom': 'http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom'}
entry = root.findall('atom:entry', ns)[0]
title = entry.find('atom:title', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
paper_id = entry.find('atom:id', ns).text.split('/abs/')[-1]
summary = entry.find('atom:summary', ns).text.strip().replace('\n', ' ')
published = entry.find('atom:published', ns).text
authors = [a.find('atom:name', ns).text for a in entry.findall('atom:author', ns)]

print("=== PAPER 1 ===")
print(f"Title: {title}")
print(f"ID: {paper_id}")
print(f"Date: {published[:10]}")
print(f"Authors: {', '.join(authors)}")
print(f"\nFull Summary:\n{summary}")

# Store paper data in a global dict
paper1 = {
    'title': title,
    'arxiv_id': paper_id,
    'summary': summary,
    'published': published,
    'authors': authors
}
```
